statements.label: supported
statements.text: Every maize m6A protein identified in the study carries the MT-A70 domain.
statements.evidence: The conserved domain analysis indicated that all identified maize m6A proteins possess the MT-A70 domain.
statements.note: The conserved domain analysis is reported as covering all identified maize m6A proteins.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Maize lines overexpressing the m6A writer genes survive drought better than wild-type plants.
statements.evidence: Furthermore, RNA-seq and RT-qPCR analysis demonstrated that the identified Zmm6A genes exhibit tissue-specific expression patterns, as well as differential expression in response to various abiotic stresses
statements.note: Only expression responses are measured; no overexpression lines or stress-tolerance phenotypes appear in the abstract.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Three m6A regulatory genes were found in the maize genome.
statements.evidence: Our analysis identified three m6A regulatory genes within the maize genome.
statements.note: The count of three regulatory genes is stated directly as a result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cold stress significantly increased the expression of ZmMTA-03 genes.
statements.evidence: Notably, the expression of ZmMTA-03 genes was significantly upregulated under cold stress conditions.
statements.note: Upregulation of ZmMTA-03 under cold stress is reported as a specific finding.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Hundreds of transcripts became markedly more abundant in neurites once HNRNPA2B1 was knocked out.
statements.evidence: we find that hundreds of RNAs demonstrate markedly increased abundance in neurites in HNRNPA2B1 knockout cells
statements.note: The increase in neurite RNA abundance in knockout cells is a reported sequencing and FISH result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Microtubule-based transport in HNRNPA2B1 knockout cells was slower and less processive.
statements.evidence: The speed and processivity of microtubule-based transport are impaired in these cells.
statements.note: Impaired speed and processivity of transport in the knockout cells is stated as a measured outcome.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Point mutants with more cytoplasmic HNRNPA2B1 suppressed RNA mislocalisation more strongly than wildtype protein did.
statements.evidence: HNRNPA2B1 point mutations that increase its cytoplasmic abundance relative to wildtype lead to stronger suppression of RNA mislocalization defects than seen with wildtype HNRNPA2B1.
statements.note: The abstract reports this direct comparison between cytoplasm-shifted point mutants and wildtype.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Neurites of HNRNPA2B1 knockout cells are shorter than those of wildtype cells.
statements.evidence: Here, we demonstrate that the RBP HNRNPA2B1 acts to keep specific RNAs out of neuronal projections.
statements.note: The abstract reports RNA abundance and transport in neurites but says nothing about neurite length or morphology.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Raising IGF2BP1 in adult erythroid cells lifts fetal hemoglobin enough to relieve sickle cell disease.
statements.evidence: This work deepens the mechanistic understanding of hemoglobin switching and suggests a physical relationship between heterochronic RBPs and globin transcripts.
statements.note: The abstract stays at the level of molecular mechanism and never mentions a disease, patients, or therapeutic benefit.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: IGF2BP1 binds HIC2 and activates it, and HIC2 itself represses BCL11A.
statements.evidence: We find that IGF2BP1 binds and activates HIC2, itself a BCL11A repressor.
statements.note: Binding and activation of the BCL11A repressor HIC2 is reported as a finding of the study.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: IGF2BP1 also acts independently of BCL11A, binding HBG1/2 directly and increasing their translation.
statements.evidence: Furthermore, we identify that IGF2BP1 plays a BCL11A-independent role by direct binding to HBG1/2 to promote its translation.
statements.note: The BCL11A-independent, translation-promoting role of direct HBG1/2 binding is stated outright.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: m6A-modified coding sequence near the HBG2 stop codon is both required and sufficient for IGF2BP1's positive regulation.
statements.evidence: Stop codon-proximal m6A-modified coding sequences within HBG2 transcripts are necessary and sufficient for direct positive regulation mediated by IGF2BP1.
statements.note: Necessity and sufficiency of these stop-codon-proximal m6A sequences is reported directly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Overexpressing circHMGB2 raised cisplatin resistance in SW1353 and OUMS-27 cells, and silencing it restored sensitivity in resistant cells.
statements.evidence: exogenous overexpression of circHMGB2 elevated cisplatin resistance in chondrosarcoma cells (SW1353, OUMS-27) in vitro, while its silencing re-sensitized resistant cells
statements.note: Both directions of the manipulation and their opposite effects on resistance are reported in the named cell lines.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: circHMGB2 worked as a competitive decoy for IGF2BP1 rather than as a miRNA sponge.
statements.evidence: circHMGB2 did not function as a miRNA sponge but acted as a competitive molecular decoy for the RNA-binding protein IGF2BP1.
statements.note: The abstract explicitly contrasts the decoy mechanism with miRNA sponging.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Circulating circHMGB2 in blood identifies chondrosarcoma patients who will not respond to cisplatin.
statements.evidence: Clinically, circHMGB2 was upregulated in chondrosarcoma tumors and associated with cisplatin resistance and poor patient survival.
statements.note: The clinical data concern circHMGB2 in tumour tissue; no blood-based measurement or prospective prediction is described.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In cisplatin-resistant xenografts, silencing circHMGB2 together with cisplatin curbed tumour growth and extended host survival.
statements.evidence: in a cisplatin-resistant xenograft model, silencing circHMGB2 synergized with cisplatin to significantly inhibit tumor growth, improve host survival, and upregulate intratumoral Grb10 while suppressing Akt phosphorylation
statements.note: The xenograft experiment reports both reduced tumour growth and improved survival from the combination.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: RBM47 was markedly more abundant in stenotic arteriovenous fistula tissue from patients and from mice alike.
statements.evidence: RBM47 expression was markedly increased in stenotic AVF tissues from both patients and mouse models.
statements.note: Increased RBM47 in stenotic AVF tissue of both species is stated as a result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Overexpressing RBM47 in endothelium made neointimal hyperplasia significantly worse.
statements.evidence: Endothelial overexpression of RBM47 significantly aggravated neointimal hyperplasia.
statements.note: Aggravation of neointimal hyperplasia by endothelial RBM47 overexpression is reported directly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: RBM47 favoured retention of SEC31A exon 13 and so cut production of the SEC31A-Δ13 splice variant.
statements.evidence: Transcriptome sequencing revealed that RBM47 promoted retention of exon 13 in SEC31A, thereby suppressing the generation of the SEC31A-Δ13 splice variant.
statements.note: Exon 13 retention and the resulting loss of the SEC31A-Δ13 variant are reported from transcriptome sequencing.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: RBM47 levels in stenotic fistula tissue rise with the time elapsed since fistula creation.
statements.evidence: RBM47 expression was markedly increased in stenotic AVF tissues from both patients and mouse models.
statements.note: The abstract reports higher RBM47 in stenotic tissue but relates it to no measure of fistula age or duration.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Under cisplatin-induced stress, IGF2BPs drive circG3BP1 into stress granules in an m6A-dependent manner.
statements.evidence: Under cisplatin-induced stress, IGF2BPs facilitate the m6A-dependent translocation of circG3BP1 to SGs
statements.note: The m6A-dependent, IGF2BP-mediated translocation of circG3BP1 into stress granules is reported as a finding.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: circG3BP1 is likewise elevated in gastric adenocarcinoma tissue.
statements.evidence: In this study, we identified m6A-modified circG3BP1 as a potential prognostic biomarker in ESCC.
statements.note: Only oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma is studied; no other tumour type is examined or mentioned.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Inside stress granules circG3BP1 scaffolds stronger TIAR-CAPRIN1 interactions and so promotes granule nucleation.
statements.evidence: where it functions as a scaffold to enhance TIAR-CAPRIN1 interactions, thereby promoting SG nucleation
statements.note: The scaffolding role and the resulting promotion of granule nucleation are stated directly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Stress granule formation lowered translation of senescence mRNAs such as p21 and delayed chemotherapy-induced senescence.
statements.evidence: SG formation suppresses the translation of senescence-associated mRNAs, such as p21, delaying chemotherapy-induced cellular senescence and contributing to cisplatin resistance in ESCC cells.
statements.note: Suppressed p21 translation and delayed senescence are reported as consequences of granule formation.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Deleting BcAGO1 and BcAGO2 together abolishes Botrytis cinerea virulence entirely.
statements.evidence: In this study, we revealed that members of fungal plant pathogen B. cinerea BcAGO family contribute to plant infection.
statements.note: A contribution of the BcAGO family to infection is reported, but no double mutant or complete loss of virulence is described.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: BcAGO1 binds small RNAs of both fungal and plant origin during infection and operates in cross-kingdom RNAi in both directions.
statements.evidence: BcAGO1 binds to both fungal and plant small RNAs during infection and acts in bidirectional cross-kingdom RNAi, from fungus to plant and vice versa.
statements.note: Binding of both small RNA pools and bidirectional cross-kingdom RNAi by BcAGO1 are stated as results.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: BcAGO2 binds fungal and plant small RNAs too, but regulates genes distinct from those controlled by BcAGO1.
statements.evidence: BcAGO2 also binds fungal and plant small RNAs but acts independent from BcAGO1 by regulating distinct genes.
statements.note: The abstract reports that BcAGO2 acts independently of BcAGO1 on a distinct set of genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Efficient delivery of pathogen small RNAs into host cells requires BcAGO2.
statements.evidence: it is required for effective pathogen small RNA delivery into host cells and fungal induced cross-kingdom RNAi
statements.note: The requirement for BcAGO2 in small RNA delivery into host cells is stated directly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Validation in three bulk transcriptomic cohorts totalling 330 samples confirmed CXCL9 and METTL14 differ between OSCC and normal tissue.
statements.evidence: Independent validation in three bulk transcriptomics cohorts (n = 330) confirmed significant differential expression of CXCL9 and METTL14 between OSCC tumor and normal tissues.
statements.note: The abstract gives the cohort count and sample number together with the confirmed differential expression.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Overexpressing METTL14 in tumour-associated macrophages increased CXCL9-positive macrophages and suppressed OSCC cell growth and stemness.
statements.evidence: In vitro, METTL14 overexpression in TAMs promoted CXCL9⁺ TAM generation and suppressed OSCC cell growth and stemness
statements.note: Both the shift towards CXCL9-positive macrophages and the suppression of growth and stemness are reported in vitro.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: OSCC patients with a high CXCL9/SPP1 ratio respond better to immune checkpoint blockade.
statements.evidence: The CXCL9/SPP1 ratio (CS ratio) has been validated as a more reliable prognostic biomarker than the conventional M1/M2 classification.
statements.note: The ratio is described as a prognostic biomarker; no treatment, and no immunotherapy response, is examined.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In macrophage-specific METTL14-knockout mice, macrophages shifted towards SPP1-positive, and tumour growth and stemness rose.
statements.evidence: METTL14 knockdown reduced m6A modification levels of CXCL9 mRNA, promoted the polarization of TAMs toward the SPP1⁺ phenotype, and ultimately accelerated OSCC tumor growth and enhanced cancer stemness
statements.note: The in vivo knockout experiment reports the SPP1-positive shift alongside faster growth and greater stemness.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cold exposure activated thermogenic metabolism in brown adipose tissue, where 7-methylguanosine was elevated.
statements.evidence: we found that cold exposure activates thermogenic metabolism in BAT and that 7-Methylguanosine is elevated in thermogenically activated BAT
statements.note: Both the metabolic activation and the raised 7-methylguanosine level come from the untargeted metabolomics result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Loss of METTL1 lowered m7G levels and weakened the thermogenic capacity of adipocytes.
statements.evidence: Loss of METTL1 reduces m 7 G levels and impairs adipocyte thermogenic capacity.
statements.note: Reduced modification levels and impaired thermogenic capacity on METTL1 loss are stated together.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Overexpressing tRF-Lys-CTT blocked brown adipocyte differentiation and thermogenic activation, while inhibiting it produced the reverse.
statements.evidence: Overexpression of tRF-Lys-CTT, which derives from an m 7 G-modified tRNA, inhibits brown adipocyte differentiation and thermogenic activation; conversely, inhibiting tRF-Lys-CTT produces the opposite effects.
statements.note: The abstract reports opposite outcomes for gain and loss of tRF-Lys-CTT.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mice lacking tRF-Lys-CTT gain less weight than controls on a high-fat diet.
statements.evidence: In summary, our study indicates that tRF-Lys-CTT functions as a post-transcriptional regulator of metabolism that suppresses thermogenesis
statements.note: The work addresses thermogenic capacity and its mechanism; no body-weight or dietary-challenge experiment is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The Dicer2 mutant showed fewer TE-derived 21nt RNAs and an altered TE expression pattern, yet TE transcript abundance did not shift much.
statements.evidence: Our results show a modified pattern of TE expression and a decrease in TE-derived 21nt RNAs in the Dicer2 mutant, but no major shift of TE transcript abundance.
statements.note: The decrease in 21nt RNAs together with unchanged overall TE transcript abundance is the reported result.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Dicer2 mutant mosquitoes are less fertile than their wild-type counterparts.
statements.evidence: We investigated the expression of TEs and small RNAs in both somatic and gonadal tissues of a Dicer2 mutant line of Ae. aegypti and its wild-type counterpart.
statements.note: The comparison with wild-type covers TE and small RNA expression; no fertility or reproductive phenotype is measured.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Without a working siRNA pathway, piRNA ping-pong signatures were perturbed with no clear sign of compensating piRNA pathway activity.
statements.evidence: The lack of a functional siRNA pathway also causes perturbations in piRNA ping-pong signatures and the expression of certain piRNA-associated genes, but without clear evidence for compensation by increased piRNA pathway activity.
statements.note: Both the perturbation and the absence of evidence for compensation are stated in the results.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Aedes aegypti does make TE-derived siRNAs, but they are not critical for TE regulation in somatic or gonadal tissue.
statements.evidence: The mosquito Ae. aegypti produces siRNAs derived from TEs but these lack a critical role in the regulation of TE expression both in somatic and in gonadal tissues.
statements.note: This is the conclusion the abstract draws for both tissue types.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The three-gene signature distinguishes ulcerative colitis from Crohn's disease.
statements.evidence: We integrated three GEO datasets and, via LASSO regression, random forest, and SVM-RFE algorithms, identified three core differentially expressed RNA methylation-related genes (DERMGs): upregulated IFIT5 and MSI2 and downregulated NCBP1.
statements.note: Diagnostic performance is reported for ulcerative colitis cohorts only; Crohn's disease is never tested or mentioned.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Among the three core RNA methylation-related genes, IFIT5 and MSI2 were raised and NCBP1 was lowered.
statements.evidence: identified three core differentially expressed RNA methylation-related genes (DERMGs): upregulated IFIT5 and MSI2 and downregulated NCBP1
statements.note: The direction of change for each of the three genes is stated explicitly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A nomogram combining all three markers reached an area under the curve of 0.947.
statements.evidence: The nomogram incorporating all three markers achieved an AUC of 0.947
statements.note: The 0.947 AUC for the three-marker nomogram is reported as a result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: LPS stimulation of NCM460 and Caco-2 colonic epithelial cells pushed IFIT5 and MSI2 up and NCBP1 down.
statements.evidence: In vitro experiments confirmed that LPS stimulation upregulated IFIT5 and MSI2 and downregulated NCBP1 in NCM460 and Caco-2 colonic epithelial cells.
statements.note: The in vitro experiment reports exactly these directions in the two named cell lines.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: FungiSNC aggregates 989 next-generation sequencing samples drawn from 29 fungal species.
statements.evidence: aggregating 989 next generation sequencing (NGS) samples from 29 fungal species
statements.note: The sample and species counts are given directly in the results.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The platform covers many small non-coding RNA classes, among them siRNAs, predicted milRNAs, phasiRNAs, snoRNAs and piRNAs.
statements.evidence: including siRNAs (small-interfering RNAs), predicted milRNAs (microRNA-like RNAs) and phasiRNAs (phased, secondary, small-interfering RNAs), rRNAs (ribosomal RNAs), tRNAs (transfer RNAs), snRNAs (small nuclear RNAs), snoRNAs (small nucleolar RNAs), piRNAs (piwi-interacting RNAs)
statements.note: All the listed classes appear in the abstract's enumeration of the categories FungiSNC covers.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Users can upload their own sRNA-seq datasets to FungiSNC and analyse them against the stored data.
statements.evidence: with all results integrated into a relational database featuring embedded analytical tools for user-friendly exploration
statements.note: Embedded tools for exploring the stored results are described, but no user data submission or upload function is mentioned.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The build pipeline preprocessed public and in-house sRNA-seq data, then detected and classified sncRNAs and annotated their function.
statements.evidence: We implemented a standardized analytical workflow encompassing (i) data preprocessing of both public repositories and in-house sRNA-seq datasets, (ii) systematic sncRNA detection and classification, and (iii) functional annotation analysis
statements.note: The three workflow stages are listed in the methods exactly in this order.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: 29% of genes carried several mammalian-conserved alternative transcripts, and 31% of those genes switched their major isoform between tissues.
statements.evidence: Our analysis reveals that 29% of genes have multiple mammalian-conserved alternative transcripts, with 31% of these genes showing tissue-specific switching of the major transcript isoforms.
statements.note: Both percentages are reported directly from the long-read atlas.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Conserved coordinated splicing was driven mainly by tissue-specific mutually associated exon splicing, most prominently in neural tissues and cytoskeletal genes.
statements.evidence: We uncover extensive conservation of coordinated splicing events, primarily driven by tissue-specific mutually associated exon splicing, particularly in neural tissues and cytoskeletal genes.
statements.note: The dominant driver and the tissues and gene class where it stands out are stated as findings.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across mammals 14.2% of m6A modifications were conserved, and 39% of the analysed genes contained a conserved m6A site.
statements.evidence: we find that 14.2% of m6A RNA modifications are conserved across mammals, with 39% of analysed genes containing a conserved m6A RNA modification
statements.note: Both epitranscriptome conservation figures are given explicitly.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Conserved m6A sites sit predominantly in the 3' UTRs of the transcripts that carry them.
statements.evidence: At the epitranscriptome level, we find that 14.2% of m6A RNA modifications are conserved across mammals, with 39% of analysed genes containing a conserved m6A RNA modification.
statements.note: Conservation is quantified, but the abstract reports nothing about where within transcripts the conserved sites lie.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Stress raised MYC mRNA in insulin-producing cells but not in alpha cells.
statements.evidence: We observed that in insulin-producing cells, but not in alpha cells, MYC mRNA levels were increased in response to stress (proinflammatory cytokines or palmitate + high glucose).
statements.note: The contrast between insulin-producing and alpha cells under stress is reported directly.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Treating MIN6 cells with PHAROH ASO 1 protected them from cytokine-induced cell death.
statements.evidence: MYC protein levels were also increased by PHAROH ASO 1, both in the absence and presence of pro-inflammatory cytokines.
statements.note: The abstract follows MYC transcript, protein and TIA1 binding after the ASO, never cell viability or apoptosis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: PHAROH ASO 1 increased both PHAROH and MYC mRNA expression in MIN6 cells.
statements.evidence: We observed that the PHAROH ASO 1 increased both PHAROH and MYC mRNA expression.
statements.note: The rise in both transcripts after PHAROH ASO 1 treatment is stated as an observation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: After PHAROH ASO 1, less MYC mRNA and more PHAROH was bound to TIA1.
statements.evidence: we observed that PHAROH ASO 1 decreased MYC mRNA binding to TIA1, and instead increased PHAROH binding to TIA1
statements.note: The reciprocal change in TIA1 binding comes from the RNA immunoprecipitation result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: ADAR2 overexpression lowered the nucleocytoplasmic ratio of TDP-43 in HEK293T cells, depending on ADAR2 catalytic activity and TDP-43 RNA binding.
statements.evidence: ADAR2 overexpression reduced the nucleocytoplasmic (N:C) ratio of TDP-43 in HEK293T cells in a ADAR2 catalytic activity- and TDP-43 RNA-binding capacity-dependent manner.
statements.note: The reduced N:C ratio and its two dependencies are reported as the primary result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Gel shift assays showed TDP-43 binds inosine-containing RNAs in preference to unedited ones.
statements.evidence: EMSAs revealed preferential binding of TDP-43 to inosine-containing RNAs relative to unedited RNAs
statements.note: The preference of TDP-43 for edited over unedited RNA is an explicit EMSA result.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Flies overexpressing dADAR in motor neurons had a shorter lifespan than control flies.
statements.evidence: Drosophila motor neurons overexpressing dADAR also exhibited decreased nuclear TDP-43.
statements.note: For these flies the abstract reports only TDP-43 localisation; survival and lifespan are not measured.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Drosophila motor neurons overexpressing dADAR held less TDP-43 in the nucleus.
statements.evidence: Drosophila motor neurons overexpressing dADAR also exhibited decreased nuclear TDP-43.
statements.note: Decreased nuclear TDP-43 in dADAR-overexpressing motor neurons is stated as a result.
